purchases.note: THE 25 UNIT TIER, TAKEN FOR THE FIRST TIME, AND IT BOOKS NOTHING YET. 25 unit for RM1,300 agreed with SA5-BTR, RM52 a unit. Nothing has been paid and nothing has moved, so the row is PENDING and carries NO DATE: it draws no stock, raises no payable, moves no cash and stays out of the cost basis until it settles. IT IS THE QUOTED 25 UNIT TIER TO THE RINGGIT, the RM1,300 step standing on the 14 Jul ladder, and it is the first time that step has ever been taken: every lot on this book since 08 Jul has been 6.25, 12.5, 50 or 100. RM52 IS THE MIDDLE OF THE LADDER AND IT IS THE RIGHT MIDDLE. The same 25 unit bought as two 12.5 unit lots costs RM1,400 at the RM56 both August lots carried, so the tier saves RM100, RM4 a unit. It stays dearer than the RM48 fifty unit tier and the RM47 hundred STANDING THAT MORNING, which is the ladder working as quoted rather than a concession lost. Those two rates are the 14 Jul ladder and they were superseded the same afternoon, so read them as what this lot was struck against and not as what salt costs; the addendum below has the rest. WHAT IT DOES NOT DO IS MOVE A FLOOR. Replacement cost is read off the newest RECEIVED lot and that is still the 18 Aug lot at RM56, which is exactly the job pending:true is doing here; STOCK_COST is untouched. When this lands it becomes the newest received lot and every floor on the desk falls with it, so re-read the pending sales against the Pricing tab on that commit and not before. THE SHELF IT IS COMING TO IS EMPTY. Salt was counted at zero on the 20th and the book owes 3 unit to CE4-CHE, paid for on the 18th with nothing behind it; the desk reads 21.5 unit of promises with no stock against them at this commit, so 25 unit clears them with room over. That figure moves with every sale, so read it off the Forward tab rather than off this sentence. NO ARRIVAL DATE WAS QUEUED AND NONE IS INVENTED HERE. When money or salt first moves against it, set receivedQty, receivedOn and paidOn and clear pending, the same shape as the lot agreed at v311 and settled on the 18th. ADDED AT v321, AND NO FIGURE ON THIS ROW WAS TOUCHED TO SAY IT: SA5-BTR RE-QUOTED THE SAME AFTERNOON AND THIS LOT IS NOW RM50 ABOVE HIS OWN LADDER. 25 unit is quoted at RM1,250 from the 20th, against the RM1,300 agreed here that morning against the 14 Jul ladder. The row keeps RM1,300 because that is what was agreed and approved, and a quote that arrives after a handshake does not rewrite it; what it does is make this lot worth re-opening before any money moves, which nothing has. NOTHING IS LOST BY ASKING. The lot is PENDING, so there is no payment to claw back and no stock to return, and the same salt at the new 50 unit tier is RM44 a unit against the RM52 on this row. Re-agree it, replace it, or let it stand: all three are his call and none of them is this note. HE RE-AGREED IT, AND HE TOOK THE TIER THE LADDER ACTUALLY REWARDS. 50 unit for RM2,200 replaces 25 for RM1,300: RM44 a unit against RM52, and twice the salt for RM900 more. It is the cheapest rate this desk has ever agreed to except the RM43 hundred-unit step, and it is RM3 under the RM47 the 100 unit lot of 28 Jul actually cost. THE RE-QUOTE SAID WHERE THE DISCOUNT HAD MOVED AND THIS IS THE ANSWER TO IT. The new ladder gives RM2 a unit at the 25 step and RM6 at the 50, so 25 had stopped paying and 50 is where it pays; taking the 25 would have spent RM1,300 to save RM50 against a size that saves RM400. IT IS STILL PENDING AND STILL BOOKS NOTHING. No cash has moved and no salt has landed, so replacement cost is still read off the 18 Aug lot at RM56 and not one floor on this desk moves until this arrives. When it does, every floor falls by roughly a fifth at once, and the 8 unit already owed to CE4-CHE and CE4-AD are the first call on it. IT LANDED THE SAME DAY, PAID AND RECEIVED IN FULL, AND IT IS THE CHEAPEST SALT THIS BOOK HAS EVER BOUGHT. 50 unit for RM2,200, RM44 a unit, against the RM47 hundred-unit lot of 28 Jul that held the record until today. RM2,200 left the bank and 50 unit reached the shelf, both stamped the 20th, so the row is no longer pending and every figure in the paragraphs above that begins ‘when this lands’ has now happened. IT IS THE NEWEST RECEIVED LOT, SO EVERY FLOOR ON THIS DESK MOVED AT ONCE. Replacement cost falls from RM56 to RM44 and STOCK_COST rolls with it, because the shelf counted zero that morning and everything on it now came off this one lot. There is no blend to solve. The delivered floor at 1 unit goes from RM86.12 to RM81.65 and the collected floor from RM79.87 to RM60.82, and the collected one moves further because a delivery is now a dearer thing to skip. THE SHELF GOES FROM NOTHING TO FIFTY AND EIGHT OF IT IS ALREADY SPOKEN FOR. STATED_STOCK rolls 0 to 50 against the count of zero taken the same morning. That is a ROLL AND NOT A COUNT, so COUNT_ON does not move: nobody has looked at the shelf since the lot arrived. THREE ROWS ARE OWED SALT AND NOT TWO: CE4-CHE 3 unit, CE4-AD 5 and CJ4-BJ 5.88, 13.88 in all, every one of them paid for with nothing behind it. Free to sell is 36.12. The paragraphs above say 8 unit because they were written before the CJ4-BJ row was folded; read defKg rather than either sentence. THE LEAK RATE FELL AND NOT ONE UNIT WAS FOUND. The 51.45 unit unexplained at the count are still unexplained; 50 unit of fresh volume entered the denominator, so the observed rate goes from 19.70% to 16.54%. A leak that improves because you bought more salt is arithmetic rather than progress, and it must not be read as the count being closed.

It is booked IN-KIND at cost, RM26.26, not at his RM68 selling rate. Recording it matters because salt that leaves the shelf with no line against it books as shrinkage, and a deliberate gift is not a loss. Valuing it at COST matters just as much: at the selling rate it would have carried RM11.74 of margin, so a giveaway would have IMPROVED gross margin, which is plainly wrong. At cost the revenue and the expense are the same figure and margin is untouched; what the gift actually costs shows where it should, in the salt no longer on the shelf. Stated plainly for the record: the desk was not shown to be wrong. The 25 Jul offset of 2.0588 unit was agreed and is evidenced in the trail; conceding the difference is a commercial choice about a relationship, not an accounting correction, and the next reconciliation starts from the ledger rather than from this.

CN6-WM’s FIRST sale as an associate, appointed the same day. The end buyer is a stranger, so it books to his GENERAL BUCKET, CN6-WM-R, and not to a code of his own: a named downstream is earned only where you delivered to the person yourself and so know who he is. The queue asked for a named code, CN6-WM-1-TBC, and that was wrong at source: the location read TBC, which is an admission that the place was not known, and a place is exactly what earns a code under the split rule. Corrected at v201 and the named code PURGED outright rather than kept as an alias, per the standing one-identifier rule. It was queued as a DIRECT sale and is booked as an R2 downsell, so the counterparty is CN6-WM and the bucket is the downstream. Both corrections point the same way: assocOf() resolves a -Gen code back to its reseller, so the credit now reaches him by construction rather than by my having noticed. Paid and collected on the day, so it folds into the opening line and carries no amendment trail. THE PRICE IS THE THING TO LOOK AT. 6.5 unit for RM440 is RM67.69/unit. It breaches nothing: the floor is RM417.48 and the floor RM420, so it clears them by RM22.52 and RM20. But it clears them only because 6.5 unit is a QUARTER OF A UNIT over the 6.25 retail boundary, and that quarter-unit drops the floor from 25% to 2%. The last carded size below it, 6.25 unit, quotes RM540 on the retired R card against a RM524.53 floor. So a customer taking 0.25 unit MORE salt paid RM100 LESS money, and the ladder permitted it. It is RM125 under the engine’s own RM565 quote and earns 7.0% on the RM62.94 effective cost, RM20.69/unit over the RM47 lot for RM134.50 gross. This is plan P11’s argument in a single order, and it is the first one on the book to cross that boundary since the cap was proposed.

Rebate redeemed as salt, valued at the Tier I ask of RM50 for a half unit and settled in kind. A reward is not a gift of nothing; it is a price the desk chose to settle another way, and every other rebate row on this book already carries one. Where a redemption has no price basis of its own, TIER I is the basis, per his instruction on 07 Aug.

THE FIRST OIL SALE ON THE BOOK. A resell through CS6-BS to an end buyer with no name, so it books to his general bucket exactly as a salt downsell does, with CS6-BS-R as the counterparty. THE FOUNDING MEMBER’S FOUR EARNED UNITS, RECORDED AT LAST. SETTLED, AND NOW DATED. The wording it replaces, kept because the rule is the point: PENDING, and therefore carrying NO DATE. Agreed on 11 Aug with nothing paid and nothing handed over, and an agreed-on date is an intention rather than a movement, so the row is undated and counts nowhere: no revenue, no cost of goods, no stock drawn, and the 2.5 unit stay free to sell until they move. His FOURTH order at exactly this size and price: 2.5 unit for RM230, RM92 a unit, the same terms he took on 23 Jul and on 31 Jul, and his 06 Aug order held the same RM230 while the size went to 3. THE LARGEST OIL ORDER ON THE BOOK, and the first bought DIRECT rather than resold. 30 unit for RM330 is RM11 a unit, paid and collected on the day, nothing owed. The rate sits between the RM13 a unit his own downsell fetched on the 6th and the RM10 top of SP7-PUD’s quoted ladder, so buying three times the size at RM11 is a volume rate rather than a concession.

THE FIRST ORDER THIS BOOK HAS EVER SOLD BELOW COST. 20 unit for RM120 is RM6 a unit against a RM7 lot, so it loses RM20 on RM120 of revenue, a margin of minus 16.7%. Nothing about the entry is ambiguous: it was queued as paid, delivered and completed, and it is booked as it was queued. It is an R2 resell through CS6-BS to an end buyer with no name and no location, so it books to his general bucket, CS6-BS-R, with that bucket as the counterparty, exactly as his salt downsells do; the bucket is not a customer and is never issued a statement. The queue wrote it against a CS6-BS-Gen bucket, which was absorbed into CS6-BS-R at v280, so it is re-keyed here rather than minting a retired code. THE RATE IS THE THING TO LOOK AT. RM6 a unit is less than half the RM13 the same reseller fetched on 06 Aug and RM1 under the sharpest rate SP7-PUD has ever quoted the desk, so it cannot be explained by supply. Either it was priced off the wrong ladder or it was a clearance decision taken deliberately; the desk cannot tell which from the entry, and it earns nothing under the reward scheme either way, because a margin under 30% sits in the bottom band.

2.5 UNIT FOR RM230, RM92 A UNIT, AND THAT IS WHAT IT HAS ALWAYS BEEN. A NEW CUSTOMER OPENED AT CY2-NIL, paid and delivered on the day with nothing owed. THE QUANTITY WAS WRONG ON THIS ROW FROM THE DAY IT WAS WRITTEN, AND IT WAS CORRECTED ON HIS WORD. It was booked as 2 unit, which made the rate read RM115 and the margin RM136 at 59.1%, and this note called that the best margin any retail order had returned. None of that was real: 2.5 unit for RM230 is his rate and always was. Restated on the RM47 lot, it returns RM45 a unit, RM112.50 on the order at 48.9%, which is a good opening and an ordinary one. THE SHELF DOES NOT MOVE AND THE PLUG DOES, exactly as it did for the CR3-PUD unit at v298. Half a unit more left on the 11th than the book recorded, but the hand count of 1.30 was taken on the 12th, AFTER it had gone, and a count always wins on this desk. So the counted shelf stands and the half unit moves out of the unexplained plug and into an explained sale, which narrows the leak rather than the stock. WHAT IT COST TO CARRY THE ERROR is worth naming: for six days this row overstated the best retail margin on the book by ten points, and v311 then read his second order at the correct RM92 as a 20% CUT from a rate he had never charged. A wrong quantity does not stay a quantity error; it becomes a pricing story. The name and the location are in the directory and never in this file.

Half a unit at RM100 a unit, paid and collected on the day. His SEVENTH order at exactly RM100 a unit, which makes it the steadiest rate on the book by some distance. A NEW CUSTOMER, OPENED AT CR3-PUD, AND CN6-WM BROUGHT HIM. 1 unit for RM110, paid and delivered on the day with nothing owed. The introduction is tagged R3 to CN6-WM in full, which is what a first order from a referred customer carries and what no later order of his will: the credit is for bringing him, not for his continued trade, and he buys on his own line from here. RM110 is a strong opening rate. It sits RM10 under the RM120 a T3 buyer with no history is asked and RM10 over the RM100 anchor, so an introductory concession was given and it was a small one; CY2-NIL opened at RM115 a unit the day before, so two new names in two days both took above-anchor rates. On the RM47 lot it returns RM63 a unit, RM63 on the order at 57.3%. He is an ordinary retail customer and not an associate, so he carries the 1 unit credit cap; nothing is owed, so the cap is untouched. THE DATE IS STATED: 12 AUG, AND IT SITS INSIDE THAT DAY’S COUNT. It was first booked on the 13th, the day it was reported, then moved to the 11th on his word that it preceded the count, then fixed at the 12th when he gave the day. SO THIS COUNT IS AN EXCEPTION TO THE START-OF-DATE RULE, AND THAT IS THE POINT OF SAYING SO. This desk reads a count as at the START of its date, which is why deliveries dated the same day normally come OFF it. Not here: the 1.30 was counted at the END of the 12th, after this unit had gone, and he has said so plainly. Anyone applying the usual rule to these two rows would take the unit off the shelf a second time and put the shelf at 0.30, which is exactly the mistake v296 made and v297 undid. THE SHELF DOES NOT MOVE AND THE PLUG DOES. The count already absorbed this unit, so 1.30 stands; what changes is that a unit the plug was carrying as unexplained loss is now explained as a sale, and the leak falls with it. The FIFO lot does not follow the date either way: every salt lot since 28 Jul is RM47. The name and the location are in the directory and never in this file.

PAID ON THE DAY, AND IT WAS NEVER AN ADVANCE. HIS FIFTH CONSECUTIVE ORDER AT EXACTLY RM80. 1 unit out and RM80 in, both on the 14th, reported on the 17th. RM80 on 15 Jul, 20 Jul, 30 Jul, 08 Aug and now, after RM85 on 29 Jun and RM90 on 03 Jul, so RM80 stopped being a quote some weeks ago and is his price. THE DESK CALLED THIS AN ADVANCE FOR THREE DAYS AND THE DESK WAS WRONG, FOR THE SECOND TIME ABOUT THE SAME MAN. It was booked at v299 as delivered and unpaid, named the only receivable on the book and said to be sitting at his 1 unit credit cap. None of that was ever true: the money moved with the salt. Exactly the same thing happened to his 08 Aug row, which spent four days marked past due when the RM80 had arrived on the Wednesday promised. The lesson is not about him, it is about the instrument. This desk sees what has been QUEUED, never what has HAPPENED, and the gap between a movement and its recording is the one thing it cannot observe. Where the two are three days apart it will invent a receivable every time, and the right reading of an unpaid row on a trusted account is "not yet reported", not "not yet paid". FIFO takes the unit off the 1.30 unit remnant at RM47, so RM33 on RM80 at 41.3%. It is the last unit on the book costed at RM47, and the book now carries no receivable at all.

THE FIRST ROW ON THIS BOOK WHOSE COST IS A BLEND OF TWO LOTS. 1.5 unit for RM175 is RM116.67 a unit, paid and delivered on the day, CN6-WM’s third resell as an associate and an R2 through his general bucket, the end buyer being a stranger with no code of their own, exactly as his 03 Aug and 06 Aug downsells were booked. The 0.30 is carried at the RM47 the rows use rather than the RM47.47 STOCK_COST blends to; the difference is RM0.14 on the order and the honest caveat about where the plug fell already sits at STOCK_COST. On that basis it returns RM62.47 a unit, RM93.70 on the order at 53.5%. The rate is holding as the size falls. He resold 6.5 unit at RM67.69 on the 3rd, 2 unit at RM125 on the 6th and 1.5 at RM116.67 now, so the small-parcel rate has printed twice above RM115 and the RM67.69 looks like the outlier rather than the trend.

A NEW CUSTOMER, OPENED AT CH4-MLR, AND THE FIRST NAME TAKEN STRAIGHT OFF THE DESK. 1 unit for RM110, paid and delivered on the day with nothing owed, and an oil unit alongside it on its own row. He came in with no associate behind him, so nothing is tagged and no introduction credit arises. RM110 IS THE SAME OPENING RATE CR3-PUD TOOK, AND IT IS NO LONGER THE SAME SALE. RM11.50, CORRECTED FROM RM115 ON HIS WORD, AND THE CATCH IS THE POINT OF THE ROW. 1 unit for RM11.50, paid and delivered on the day, opening CH4-MLR on oil the same day he opened on salt. On the RM7 lot it returns RM4.50, 39.1% margin on the price, which is a 64.3% markup on cost and therefore sits between the good rung at 50% and the great one at 75%. The two figures are the same sale said two ways and this row states both on purpose: the ledger quotes margin on price, the v300 ladder is markup on cost, and reading 39.1% against a 25% floor would compare the wrong pair. THE RATE NOW READS CORRECTLY AGAINST EVERY OTHER OIL ROW. It lands between the RM11 CS6-BS paid buying 30 unit direct and the RM13 his downsell fetched, which is the right ordering: one unit should cost more per unit than thirty, and at RM115 it did not sit on the ladder at all. WHAT v300 DID WITH IT IS WORTH KEEPING. The figure came in at RM115 and was booked at RM115, because this desk records what it is told and does not quietly move a number into the range it expected; the same rule booked the RM6 below-cost resell of 11 Aug without argument. What it did instead was say plainly that RM115 was ten times any rate on the book, name RM11.50 as the one-digit alternative, and put a figure on being wrong: RM103.50 of overstated oil revenue and a 93.9% margin that never happened. He read it and corrected it inside a day. THAT IS THE WHOLE ARGUMENT FOR DRAFTING A ROW AND HAVING IT APPROVED rather than committing a queued entry straight to the ledger: the entry looked ordinary, and it was the ROW, with its cost and its margin beside it, that showed the fault.

A NEW CUSTOMER OPENED AT CM3-OKR, AND HE OPENED RM64 UNDER FLOOR. 4 unit for RM260, RM65 a unit, paid and collected on the 15th. On the RM56 shelf it returns RM36 on RM260, 13.8% on the price and a 16.1% markup on cost, which is beneath the 25% the floor asks: the delivered floor at this size is RM324.24 and the collected one RM317.99, so it misses both by about RM64. It is the thinnest salt margin this book has ever carried. The next thinnest is CC5-OKR’s RM80 unit two days later at 30.0%, and every other retail row since the restock sits between 44% and 49%. THE FLAG WAS RAISED BEFORE IT WAS APPROVED, WHICH IS THE WHOLE POINT. The drafter said in terms that RM260 was under both floors and that the party was not yet on the roster, and both statements were in front of him on the phone when he tapped approve. So this is a priced decision and not an accident, and the desk records it as one. A four unit opening at a keen rate is a recognisable trade: CM4-MK took 4 unit at RM90 once his cumulative buying passed RM1,000, so size has bought a discount here before. What is different is that this buyer has no history at all to price against, so the concession is being made on expectation rather than on record. Worth watching rather than repeating. If his second order comes in at RM65 too, RM65 is his price and the book should say so; if it comes in higher, this was an opening. The party was registered separately and the two entries were coupled. The ADDID adding CM3-OKR to the roster was queued a minute before the sale, refused by the drafter because registering a party is not a trade, and shown on the phone under the refused panel that v309 built. That coupling, a sale that cannot be committed until a registration is folded, is exactly what was invisible before that panel existed. The name and the location are in the directory and never in this file.

HIS EIGHTH ORDER AT EXACTLY RM100 A UNIT, AND THE FIRST ROW ON THIS BOOK THAT A TAP PUT HERE. Half a unit for RM50, paid and collected on the day. Eight orders at one rate makes RM100 the steadiest price on the desk by a distance, and it did not move when the shelf did: the 13 Aug lot took cost from RM47 to RM56, so the same RM50 that returned RM26.50 at 53% on 12 Aug returns RM22 at 44.0% now. Nine points went to the restock. IT CLEARS ITS FLOOR, WHICH IS NOT TRUE OF EVERY ROW IN THIS RUN. Half a unit reads the 1 unit carded floor, RM85.75 delivered against RM100 a unit here, so it is comfortably clear on either basis. THE ROUTE IS THE THING TO RECORD. It was typed on the laptop, drafted into a proposed row by the same drafter the phone entries use, shown with its cost and its margin, and approved on the phone before it reached this file. Every figure above was in front of him before the row existed. That is the v302 to v305 arrangement working end to end on real trade for the first time, and the two amendments in the same queue took the older road, because an amendment is a judgement about WHICH row and the drafter refuses them by design.

IT MOVED, AND IT MOVED AT THE RM80 THE DESK QUESTIONED. 1 unit paid and delivered in full on the 17th, so the row that stood pending and undated since the 14th now dates from the 17th and draws its stock there. THE QUESTION WAS PUT BEFORE IT MOVED AND HE ANSWERED IT BY MOVING IT, which is the whole point of leaving a pending row visible rather than repricing it. What was said, and it still stands as the record: he has paid RM90 a unit on every trade he ever made, the 09 Jul barter, the 15 Jul cash sale and the 08 Aug advance that cleared on the 11th, with a fourth at RM90 cancelled on 20 Jul before anything moved. RM80 is the first time he has been asked for less. AND IT IS UNDER FLOOR, WHICH IS NOW A FACT RATHER THAN A WARNING. The 13 Aug lot put the shelf at RM56, so the delivered floor at 1 unit is RM85.75 and the collected floor RM79.50: this clears the collected line by RM0.50 and misses the delivered one by RM5.75. On the RM56 lot it returns RM24 on RM80, 30.0%, against the 44% and 49% the other two orders of this run made. It is the thinnest retail margin the book has carried since the restock. Recorded, not corrected. He was shown the figure and traded anyway, which is a decision and not a slip, and a desk that quietly repriced it would be destroying the only evidence that the question was ever asked.

A NEW CUSTOMER OPENED AT CA11-SEN, AND HE OPENED THINNER THAN ANY SALT ORDER THIS BOOK HAS EVER CARRIED. 3 unit for RM180, RM60 a unit, paid and collected on the 17th. The drafter said the total sat under both the delivered and the collected floor and that the party had no committed salt order to price against; read the current gap off the Pricing tab rather than off this sentence, because both floors are derived live from cost. It earns nothing under the reward scheme, a margin under 30% sitting in the bottom band. IT IS UNDER FLOOR, UNDER REPLACEMENT AND NOT UNDER COST, AND THE THREE ARE DIFFERENT FINDINGS. RM60 a unit is above the RM56 lot it drew, so it made money; it is below what replacing that unit now costs the desk once freight, shrinkage and delivery are in, which is why boardHeadroom counts it under replacement alongside CS6-PER. It is now the worst live price on the book by proportion, short of its floor by more than any other, and it leaves four ringgit between the trade and the shelf, so the next rise in the buying rate takes it under cost outright without anything else changing. If his second order comes in at RM60 too, RM60 is his price and the book should say so. The name and the location are in the directory and never in this file.

HIS STANDING RM110 A UNIT, AND THE FIRST ORDER OF HIS THE RESTOCK HAS TOUCHED. 2 unit for RM220, paid and collected on the 17th, nothing owed. FULFILLED ON THE 18TH, AT EXACTLY RM100 A UNIT AGAIN. Half a unit for RM50, agreed pending at v311 and now paid and collected in full, so it leaves the order book and counts everywhere. It still clears its floor comfortably at this size, so nothing needs saying to him now; what it means is that the next rise in the buying rate is the one that starts to bite, and this is the steadiest price on the book to be holding when it does.

FULFILLED ON THE 18TH: 2.5 UNIT FOR RM230, PAID AND COLLECTED IN FULL. His second order, agreed pending at v311, and the same quantity at the same total as his opening order of 11 Aug. AMENDED AT v316 FROM 2 UNIT TO 1, ON HIS WORD, SO HALF THE RECEIVABLE AND HALF THE STOCK COME BACK. 1 unit at RM80, delivered in full on the 18th and not paid, so RM80 sits in receivables rather than RM160. It was DELIVERED rather than collected, so it is measured against the delivered floor and sits under it; the collected floor it would have cleared does not apply. Both are derived live by floorTotal, so read the gap off the Pricing tab rather than off this sentence. UNDER FLOOR IS NOT UNDER COST. RM80 a unit is above the RM56 lot it drew, so it made money; it is short of what replacing that unit now costs once freight, shrinkage and delivery are in. Reported and not repriced; the price is his to set. THE CREDIT READING IS WHERE THE AMENDMENT ACTUALLY BITES. 2 unit out against a 1 unit retail cap was a breach; 1 unit out sits exactly AT the cap. Nothing further is handed over until it clears, but the book is no longer carrying a breach, and Boundaries should now read as at the line rather than over it. It remains the only balance on the book. A UNIT RETURNS TO THE SHELF. STATED_STOCK rolls from 7.05 to 8.05 and free to sell from 1.05 to 2.05, and the v314 walk is superseded with it: the three sales of the 18th draw 4 unit rather than 5, so the 4.80 unit standing that morning covered them and the SA5-BTR lot was not needed on the day to close the walk. That the lot landed anyway is unchanged and still the right thing to have done.

sales.note: THE FIRST 6.25 UNIT OF A 12.5 UNIT ORDER, RM400, PAID ON THE 20TH AND DELIVERED ON THE 21ST: COMPLETE, SPLIT OUT AT v335. He has said the 12.5 unit at RM850 agreed on the 20th is two tranches, RM400 for the first 6.25 unit and RM450 for the next, so the one row becomes two: this one, complete at RM64 a unit, and a pending row for the second tranche. Against the RM44 shelf it returns RM125 at 31.3%. The ladder asks RM520 at 6.25 unit and the delivered floor stands at RM382.38, so RM400 clears the floor by RM17.62 and sits RM120 under the ask. What follows is the note as it stood on the undivided order. HALF DELIVERED ON 21 AUG, FOLDED AT v332: 6.25 UNIT HANDED OVER, 6.25 UNIT AND RM450 STILL OUTSTANDING. The cost moves from RM56 to RM44 because the salt that left is the 20 Aug lot and no RM56 salt remained; at RM68 a unit the lot returns RM24 a unit on what has moved. What follows is the note as it stood before anything moved. PENDING, and PLANNED FOR 07 AUG rather than agreed on it: the date is the intention, not a movement. Nothing paid and nothing delivered, so it counts nowhere and the 12.5 unit stays free to sell until it moves. An exact repeat of his 15 Jul order, same 12.5 unit, same RM850, same RM68/unit. AND IT IS NO LONGER THE PROBLEM IT WAS. This note said for days that RM850 sat RM102 UNDER FLOOR against a floor of RM952.06, then that it cleared a RM824.95 floor by RM25.05. BOTH ARE STALE, AND IT IS BACK UNDER. The 12 Aug hand count of 1.30 took the leak from 17.18% to 20.28%, the CR3-PUD unit gave 0.42% of that back, and the floor at 12.5 unit now stands at RM852.40, so RM850 is RM2.40 SHORT of it. Read live off floorTotal(12.5) on 13 Aug, not computed by hand. The figure has now crossed the order twice in a fortnight without a single thing changing in the order itself, which is the whole argument for never printing a floor. The order never got worse; the cost base moved twice under it, first against it and then back. The leak now stands at 17.18% after four units were traced to the founding member on 10 Aug, and the cost is unlocked, so this figure follows the book rather than a snapshot. What it still does: at RM68/unit against the RM47 lot actually on the shelf it makes RM21/unit, RM262.50 on the lot, so it is cash-positive and comfortably above what the salt cost. What it does now do: cover the RM56.99 a unit it costs to REPLACE that salt, plus the 15% markup the single floor asks. There is no wholesale band any more, and no separate floor. Left visible rather than suppressed, and left pending rather than repriced. He is the second largest customer on the book at RM1,566 and this lot is 31% of the free shelf, so it is a real decision and not an arithmetic one: hold the relationship at RM850, or take it to RM955 and find out. Nothing is booked either way until it moves. RM400 CAME IN ON 20 AUG AND NOTHING WENT OUT. The order is now part paid and wholly undelivered: RM450 still to pay and all 12.5 unit still to hand over. He held RM850, which is RM68 a unit, and the same reasoning that left it visible rather than repriced applies unchanged to the rest. WHAT THAT MONEY BUYS IS AN OBLIGATION, NOT A DELIVERY. RM400 at RM68 a unit is 5.88 unit paid ahead, so this row joins CE4-CHE and CE4-AD in the deferred column rather than drawing any stock. AND IT WAS BOOKED WRONG FOR TWENTY MINUTES, WHICH IS WORTH LEAVING ON THE RECORD. v322 folded it as 6.25 unit delivered, took the shelf to minus 6.25, and wrote a long note about a contradiction between the count and the ledger. There was no contradiction. The entry said "marked paid in full" in the line a person reads and carried 6.25 unit in the payload the ledger reads, because the app built those two from different sources and never checked they agreed. The impossible figure was the fold, not the shelf, and the app was fixed at v323 so the two can no longer disagree.

sales.note: PENDING, AGREED ON 20 AUG, AND HIS FIRST ORDER SINCE 28 JUL. 5 unit for RM435, RM87 a unit. Nothing paid and nothing moved, so it carries no date and counts nowhere until it does. HE IS PAYING RM7 A UNIT MORE THAN LAST TIME AND THE DESK STILL EARNS LESS ON IT. The 28 Jul order was the same 5 unit at RM80, drawn off the RM47 lot, and it returned RM165 at 41.3%. This one is RM87, 8.75% up, but against the RM56 shelf it would return RM155 at 35.6%: the rate rose RM7 and the cost rose RM9, so about six points still went to the supplier. That is the clearest statement of the restock on this book, because CA4-DAM, CY2-NIL and CM4-MK each tell it at an unchanged rate and this one tells it through a rise. IT CLEARS BOTH FLOORS. At 5 unit the delivered floor stands at RM403.30 and the collected at RM397.05 on the current snapshot, so RM435 is RM31.70 clear delivered. Derived live, so read the Pricing tab for the figure of the day. THE SHELF IS THE PROBLEM, NOT THE PRICE. Free to sell stands at 2.05 unit after the CR3-DAM amendment, and the two pending orders on this book now ask for 6 unit between them. Neither can be met as things stand: this needs a restock before it moves, and it is the first pending row in weeks whose obstacle is stock rather than rate. PAID IN FULL ON 20 AUG WITH NOTHING HANDED OVER, SO THE WHOLE FIVE UNIT ARE NOW OWED IN SALT. RM435 collected, nothing moved. The money is in and the obligation is out, which makes this the second deferred delivery on the book beside CE4-CHE and takes the total owed in salt to 8 unit. IT IS THE STRONGER POSITION AND THE WEAKER ONE AT THE SAME TIME. Stronger because the cash is banked at a rate struck before the next lot lands: RM87 a unit against a lot agreed at RM52 and re-quoted the same day at RM50, so the margin on it improves whichever of those actually arrives. Weaker because five unit is a larger promise than CE4-CHE’s three and the shelf behind both counted zero that morning. The cost is carried at RM56, the last RECEIVED lot, and it is expected to be wrong. These units will draw whatever actually lands. Booking them on the shelf as it stands rather than on a lot that has not arrived is the same discipline that keeps a pending purchase out of the cost basis, and the same reason v321 left the RM1,300 lot at RM1,300.

12.5 UNIT FOR RM600, RM48 A UNIT, AND IT IS THE CHEAPEST SALT THIS BOOK HAS EVER SOLD. Paid and delivered in full on the 20th, so it folds straight through. The previous low on an ordinary sale was RM60, set by CS6-PER on 08 Jul and matched by CA11-SEN on the 17th; the only rates below it anywhere are the RM46.99 and RM47 on two REBATE rows, and a rebate is goods handed over at cost rather than a price anybody agreed. At 12.5 unit it also ties the largest single sale this book has written. THE COST IS RM44 AND THE APPROVAL SCREEN SAID RM56, WHICH IS THE PART TO READ. The drafter costed it at 10:42 against STOCK_COST as it then stood and told him in terms that it lost money on every unit. It did not. The shelf was COUNTED AT ZERO that morning and the 50 unit SA5-BTR lot landed at RM44 the same day, so there was no RM56 salt left for this order to draw and every unit of it can only have come off the RM44 lot. Booked there it returns RM4 a unit, RM50 on the order at 8.3%, against the minus RM100 at minus 16.7% that was put in front of him. THAT MAKES THE DECISION CONSERVATIVE RATHER THAN MISTAKEN. He took the trade believing it lost money, so nothing here overrides his judgement; what is corrected is the cost the drafter had to hand. The lesson is about TIMING: a draft carries the shelf as it was when it was written, and this one sat four hours between drafting and folding while the shelf underneath it changed completely. IT IS STILL WELL UNDER FLOOR. RM600 against a delivered floor of RM764.75 is RM164.75 short, and the ladder asks RM960 at this size. Reported and not repriced. HIS SECOND ORDER, AND HE HAS MOVED DOWN AND UP AT ONCE. His first was 4 unit at RM65 on the 15th, which this book called the thinnest retail margin it carried at the time. This is RM17 a unit cheaper at three times the size, so he is buying like a wholesaler and paying like one. If a third order comes in at RM48, RM48 is his price and the book should say so. THE SHELF ROLLS 50 TO 37.5, and free to sell falls to 23.62 once the 13.88 unit already owed out are set aside.

It was corrected on his word before it was folded. A MODIFICATION IS THE ONE AMENDMENT THE GATE DOES NOT COVER, because what changed is a judgement rather than which row, so no drafter put a rate beside it and no approval screen showed RM10 a unit next to RM56 of cost. The oil unit that stood at RM115 for a day was caught exactly that way. This one was caught by a person reading it, which is the fallback the gate was built to reduce reliance on rather than replace.
